audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer tracks a fabricated ability, 'Twofold Hunt', and even labels it '(Blink)'. The content layer invents a second one: 'her W exile root'. Both layers also treat E as the escape.
audit.why: Aurora's Q is Twofold Hex — a missile that curses enemies and is recast to drag the curses back. Nothing in her kit roots: W Across the Veil is 'leaps in a direction of her choosing, entering the spirit realm upon landing, becoming invisible', E The Weirding 'damages and slows enemies before Aurora hops backward', R Between Worlds damages and slows. The escape is W at 22s rank 1, not E at 15s and not Q.
audit.corrected: Twofold Hunt replaced with Twofold Hex, the invented W root removed, and the escape correctly attributed to Across the Veil with its 22s rank-1 cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer calls Aurora 'him' and 'his' throughout, and report[2] says 'No permanent owner here' while both charts give her four of seven stages. phases[0].why and breakdown.early both credit Galio with a 'passive shield'.
audit.why: Galio's passive is Colossal Smash, a periodic empowered area auto-attack — he has no passive shield. The shield is on W and R.
audit.corrected: Pronouns fixed in every edited line, the passive-shield claim deleted, and the chart summary matched to the recorded stages.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[5].why calls Stormsurge/Riftmaker 'your spike' on a stage the chart gives Aurora, phases[4].why ends in the boilerplate 'Reassess his ultimate too', and no cooldowns appear anywhere.
audit.why: Across the Veil 22s at rank 1, The Weirding 15s, Twofold Hex 9s at 900 range, Between Worlds 140s. Against Galio's 825-range Q, her 900-range Q is the whole early-lane story.
audit.corrected: Every stage line now names the ability and cooldown that owns it.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three places tell the player to 'R-isolate to deny it'. Hero's Entrance does not isolate anyone.
audit.why: Hero's Entrance designates an ally's position, shields allies in the area, and after a delay knocks up nearby enemies. It has no isolation or escape-denial component.
audit.corrected: Replaced with the real escape rule — punish on Across the Veil's cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: Anti-heal appears nowhere in the content layer even though her passive heals.
audit.why: Spirit Abjuration: 'Aurora's spells and attacks exorcise spirits from the enemies she damages. Exorcised spirits follow Aurora around and heal her.' A poke lane against a self-healing mage is exactly where Oblivion Orb changes the maths.
audit.corrected: Oblivion Orb written into the late text, the first-item stage, whys[5] and the itemization slot.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns carried no durations and pointed at the fabricated ability.
audit.why: Across the Veil's 22s at rank 1 is the longest window Aurora ever gives a Galio, and it is the only one worth waiting for.

edits.before: Level 1 is a wash — you have one ability and no engage, she has Q poke but no all-in either, so just last-hit and respect her range. From level 2 she takes over: her Q windblasts chip you while you have no way to retaliate, and the moment you wind up Justice Punch she blinks with E so your knockup hits air. Don't throw a desperate E into her — bait the blink, eat a little poke, and farm. Your Winds of War tornado can contest the wave and zone her off a cannon, but she out-pokes you in a straight stand-off through level 3.
edits.after: Level 1 is a wash — you have one ability and no engage, she has Twofold Hex poke but no all-in either, so last-hit and respect her 900 range. From level 2 she takes over: the hex chips you while you have no way to retaliate, and the moment you wind up Justice Punch she leaps Across the Veil and goes invisible, so your knockup hits air. Don't throw a desperate E — bait the leap, eat a little poke, and farm. Winds of War can contest the wave and zone her off a cannon, but she out-pokes you in a straight stand-off through level 3.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 still belong to her — her Q poke plus W exile root out-damages your extended trades and her E keeps her out of Shield of Durand's taunt range, so don't force a fight you'll lose. Then 6 changes everything: Hero's Entrance is your equalizer. You don't need to win the 1v1 — shove the wave, channel R onto mid or bot, and turn a lane you're losing into two lanes you're winning. If you DO commit on her, only E-in after her E blink is spent, then the W-release taunt locks her down for your full combo since she has nothing left to escape with.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 still belong to her — Twofold Hex chip plus The Weirding's slow out-damages your extended trades and Across the Veil keeps her out of Shield of Durand's taunt range, so don't force a fight you'll lose. Then 6 changes everything: Hero's Entrance is your equalizer. You don't need to win the 1v1 — shove the wave, channel R onto mid or bot, and turn a lane you're losing into two lanes you're winning. If you DO commit, only E-in after Across the Veil is spent; on a 22s cooldown she has nothing left, and the W-release taunt locks her for your full combo.

edits.before: This is where you reclaim the matchup. With one MR item, Shield of Durand's magic-amplified damage reduction shrugs off her Q-W burst, so her poke stops mattering and you can walk her down whenever her E is on cooldown. More importantly you're a teamfight and roam machine — Hero's Entrance drops you onto her carry from across the map, knocking up and taunting through her squishy backline. She scales as a skirmisher, but you don't lose to her late; you out-utility her by being everywhere with R while she's stuck winning a single side lane.
edits.after: This is where you reclaim the matchup. With one MR item, Shield of Durand's magic-amplified damage reduction shrugs off her Twofold Hex burst, so her poke stops mattering and you can walk her down whenever Across the Veil is on its 22s. Add Oblivion Orb, because Spirit Abjuration heals her off the spirits your chip keeps creating. More importantly you're a teamfight and roam machine — Hero's Entrance drops you onto her carry from across the map, knocking up and taunting through her squishy backline. She scales as a skirmisher, but you out-utility her by being everywhere with R.

notes: aurora.json flags Between Worlds (R) with 'hardCC', but Riot's description only gives damage and slows — no stun or root — so I described it as a slow zone and made no hard-CC claim. The content layer's 'W exile root' had no basis in any local file.
